plans.note: Only the preamble is exposed in the outline; a Master Services Agreement of this type almost always carries a limitation of liability article. Scan the full body text under sec-preamble for cap amount, mutuality and carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence).

Search the body for Kubient's indemnity covering third-party IP claims and its own negligence/willful misconduct, and confirm any AP-side indemnity is narrow (limited to AP-supplied content). Treat as missing only if no indemnity language appears anywhere.

Presence rule; restrictions on AP's ability to operate competing businesses are uncommon in a vendor MSA. Confirm by scanning any restrictive-covenant or 'Other Agreements' language before concluding absent.
Check the services/scope and term provisions for any 'sole' or 'exclusive' supplier wording binding AP; otherwise absent and no comment needed.
Direction rule; look in fees/pricing text for any obligation on AP to give Kubient best terms. An MFN running in AP's favour is welcome and should not be flagged.
Ad-tech MSAs frequently include a mutual non-solicit. Check duration (12 months preferred), scope (employees involved in the engagement) and the general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out.

Term and termination provisions should sit in the body under sec-preamble; check whether AP has termination for convenience on notice without penalty and whether Kubient has a symmetrical mid-term exit (which we resist). Note interaction with Initial Term.

'Initial Term' is a defined term, so renewal mechanics are almost certainly present; check auto-renewal length, the non-renewal notice window (30 days preferred, 60 acceptable) and any price-uplift cap.

Look for the miscellaneous/general provisions at the end of the body; Kubient is New York-based so New York law with New York courts is likely and acceptable. Flag only foreign law or mandatory offshore arbitration.
Check the general provisions for AP's right to assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger without consent, and for any Kubient termination right triggered by AP's change of control.

Direction rule; confirm AP retains ownership of AP content/data and of paid-for deliverables, and that any licence to Kubient is limited to performing the services. Watch for feedback or aggregated-data assignments running to Kubient.
Check the grant of rights to AP for the platform/services: it should extend to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf and must not be revocable at Kubient's discretion.

Look for records/audit language; assess frequency (annual), advance notice, business-hours limits, and whether Kubient bears its own audit cost absent a material discrepancy. Do not flag audit rights running in AP's favour.
Direction rule; scan fees and termination text for early-termination fees, penalties or liquidated damages payable by AP. Service credits or remedies flowing to AP are welcome and not flagged.
Check the warranties article for a professional/workmanlike services warranty of meaningful duration with re-performance or refund as the remedy, and note any broad 'AS IS' disclaimer that guts it.

Kubient handles AP data through its platform, so an insurance covenant (CGL, E&O/tech, cyber) is expected; treat as missing only if no insurance obligation appears in the body or any exhibit referenced from it.
Presence rule; check the fees/order-form language for minimum spend, take-or-pay or volume floors on AP. Likely absent in a revenue-share style ad-tech MSA but confirm before concluding.

Check effect-of-termination/survival language for return or deletion of AP data in a usable format and for transition assistance at agreed rates; flag as missing if only deletion (and no return or assistance) is addressed.
